Issue #3044 asks for a preprocess-only mode that keeps comments. The source
below is a small pixel shader with one deliberate property: the text carried in
its comments appears nowhere else in the file, and the body relies on a macro,
so a successful preprocess is distinguishable from a copy of the input.

The panes do not show a preprocess run, because they cannot: dxc writes
preprocessed text to a file rather than to stdout, so a plain preprocess-only
run answers "<No output file>" here and shows nothing. What the panes do show
is the question that actually decides this request -- whether the flag exists
at all. Each pane appends clang's comment-retention flag, in the spelling that
build's option grammar accepts, and each answers "Unknown argument". The flag
is absent from dxc's option table from the oldest build Compiler Explorer
offers through trunk.

Locally, the underlying capability is present: clang's preprocessor supports
comment retention, and dxc's driver hardcodes it off when it builds the
preprocessor output options. Only the driver-side plumbing is missing.

Compiler Explorer runs Linux Release builds; they corroborate the Windows
Debug build used for triage and never overrule it.
